title: Mutually Recursive Parsers with Forward Cells
description: Introduce a callable Forward placeholder class so mutually recursive grammar rules like expr, term, and factor can reference each other before their bodies are set.

steps.description: Include the inline combinators satisfy, regex, lit, seq, alt, many, pmap, and token.
Define Forward with self._inner = None, a set(self, p) method to wire in the actual parser later, and __call__(self, s, i) to delegate to self._inner(s, i).

steps.question: Why can factor.set(...) on line 79 pass expr into seq(lparen, expr, rparen) before expr.set(...) has been called?
steps.answer: Because expr is already a Forward object, seq stores a reference to that Forward object now and only calls expr(s, i) later at parse time after expr.set(build_expr) has populated expr._inner.

steps.description: Create Forward instances for expr, term, and factor, define the lexical tokens, and set factor to match either number or a parenthesized expr.
Wire build_term into term.set and build_expr into expr.set to evaluate *, /, +, and - left to right at their respective precedence levels, then run the test expressions.
Watch factor.set wire the parenthesized expr reference into the factor parser.
